title: Optimisation in practice: conditioning, momentum, mini-batches and adaptive methods
summary: Quadratic conditioning, momentum recurrences, stochastic-gradient sampling, adaptive updates and controlled optimisation comparisons.

objectives.description: Analyse conditioning and stability on positive-definite quadratics.
Derive momentum recurrences with a consistent state convention.
Compute mini-batch expectation and variance under stated sampling rules.
Audit adaptive updates and compare optimisation methods without contaminating evaluation.

preparation.description: Read sections4,6,7 on conditioning, momentum, mini-batches and adaptive methods; record the update and epsilon conventions.

activities.title: Lecture notes and primary reading
activities.instructions: Work through the notes with the assigned source open. Reproduce each worked calculation or derivation on paper, including its assumptions, before reading the next step. Write one question that remains unresolved.

activities.title: Problem sheet: calculation, explanation and transfer
activities.instructions: Attempt the problems independently first. Use one hint at a time if useful, and record which help you used. Show the reasoning that connects the model and its assumptions to each answer; compare the reference only after a substantial attempt.

activities.title: Return without the notes
activities.instructions: On a later study day, close the notes and reconstruct the core relation and its assumptions, then explain the failure case from the last problem. Compare with your saved work and correct one gap. This practice does not itself certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to judge the objectives: explain assumptions, complete the independent calculations and justify the final transfer/synthesis. The final exercise is the recorded checkpoint; its acceptance alone is not a claim that all course outcomes are mastered.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A stable run from one initial point proves a step size is safe.
commonMisconceptions.correction: An unstable eigenmode may be absent from that initial point.

commonMisconceptions.claim: The moving mean of squared gradients is always their variance.
commonMisconceptions.correction: It is a second moment; variance also subtracts the squared mean.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Adaptive optimisation removes the need for validation-based tuning.
commonMisconceptions.correction: It still has hyperparameters, costs and failure modes; test data must remain separate.
